source.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization with Adaptive Regularization for Training Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Jinping Zou; Xiao-Ge Deng; Tao Sun

record.file_problem: Full text supplied, including appendix; no apparent truncation affecting the reported experiments.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training and test accuracy-derived generalization error for several optimizers, including a refinement that adaptively adjusts SAM regularization. The results bear on optimizer-related generalization under the tested settings.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 optimizer comparisons. Its method uses SAM-style sharpness regularization, but it does not test memorization of random labels, width scaling, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness versus other measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization premise to develop SAMAR and reports its optimizer's performance. It tests none of V1–V8: adaptive regularization is not an Adam-style adaptive optimizer comparison, and optimizing unscaled sharpness does not test whether magnitude-aware sharpness ranks generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: SAMAR has a convergence rate aligned with SAM and improves accuracy and generalization in their CIFAR experiments, particularly for larger models on the more complex dataset, while sometimes trailing VaSSO. This is not universal superiority across metrics, and no formal significance test is reported.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces an adaptive regularization parameter within a SAM-style optimizer; compares SAMAR with SGD, SAM and VaSSO on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. The text states all methods use weight decay 0.0005; training uses data augmentation and 100 epochs.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state SAMAR may lag behind VaSSO in certain scenarios; they attribute some CIFAR-10 metric differences to the dataset's relatively small scale and models being easily overfitted.

fits_no_version.finding: SAMAR has a smaller mean train–test accuracy gap than SGD and SAM in all four dataset–architecture combinations. Against VaSSO, its gap is smaller in three combinations but larger for ResNet-34 on CIFAR-10: 2.625 versus 2.580 percentage points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive sharpness regularization can improve generalization gaps relative to SGD and SAM in these augmented, weight-decayed CIFAR training recipes, with advantages over VaSSO depending on the setting.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
record.problems: Experiments use two CIFAR datasets, two model architectures, 100 epochs, batch size 256 and three independent runs. The main tables are flattened, though the text specifies max, mean±std format. CIFAR-10 results include cases where SAMAR is not best; the authors acknowledge it may lag VaSSO in some scenarios.

untested.parts: No random-label training or comparison with natural-label generalization.
No controlled width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No Adam-style adaptive gradient method versus SGD comparison under either limited or broader tuning.
Batch size is fixed at 256; no batch-size or compensating-recipe comparison.
No dropout intervention or dropout-by-training-set-size comparison.
No measurement of magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, correlation with generalization gaps, or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
No memorization-based example selection, removal, or retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: All row states concern applicability to V1–V8, not whether the reported gaps are readable. The gaps are readable after separating maximum and mean±standard deviation across three runs. These are method-evaluation rows and should not enter the evidence set for these versions. References to V5 and V7 findings in related work are cited results, not new tests.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural labels are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No fully connected versus convolutional comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
The optimizer comparison includes SGD and SAM variants, not adaptive methods such as Adam, and does not evaluate the stated tuning conditions.
No measurement of magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of generalization measures.
No removal or retraining of memorized examples.
